subject.title: Granola 7.427.2 moved the DEK from storage.dek into the macOS Keychain — encrypted-json/private-api unlock fails with "read storage.dek: no such file or directory"

question: Should graincrawl treat Granola 7.427+ encrypted state as an explicitly unsupported upstream boundary, or pursue an authorized companion mechanism for retrieving the access-group-protected DEK?
rationale: Ordinary Keychain access cannot safely or reliably bypass another application's signed access group, and selecting a helper, entitlement, or app bridge changes the credential-access trust boundary.

options.title: Diagnose and fail closed
options.body: Add precise Doctor and unlock diagnostics now, document the limitation, and avoid attempting to bypass Granola's Keychain access group.

options.title: Pursue supported bridge
options.body: Investigate a Granola-provided companion API or authorized helper, requiring explicit provenance, threat-model review, and live macOS proof before implementation.

recommendation.title: Diagnose and fail closed
recommendation.body: Add precise Doctor and unlock diagnostics now, document the limitation, and avoid attempting to bypass Granola's Keychain access group.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice affects the repository's core local-data and credential-access boundary and is best routed to the likely crawler feature owner.
